stem: In a child with hypospadias, what is chordee and how often does it occur?

options.text: An infection of the urethral plate seen in 5% of cases
A ventral deficiency of the foreskin seen in 50% of cases
A degree of penile bend seen in 20-25% of cases
The presence of undescended testes seen in 10% of cases
A narrowing of the urethral meatus seen in most cases

explanation: Chordee is a penile curvature associated with hypospadias, and it occurs in about 20-25% of cases.
rationale: Chordee refers to the curved penis seen in some children with hypospadias, not an infection, foreskin abnormality, or testicular anomaly.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because chordee is a structural curvature of the penis, not an infection of the urethral plate.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a ventral hooded or deficient foreskin may occur with hypospadias, but chordee specifically refers to penile bending.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because chordee is the penile curvature associated with hypospadias and occurs in about 20-25% of cases.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because undescended testes are a separate condition and do not define chordee.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because meatal narrowing can be seen in hypospadias, but chordee refers to curvature of the penis rather than the urethral opening.

source.hint: Identify the term for the physical curvature of the penis and its statistical prevalence in hypospadias patients.
